comment: Anatomical parts inside each muscle group, used by evs/muscle_sculpt.py to sculpt each part as its own block with a groove between parts (Kiệt 14/11: muscles drawn as separate layered blocks that follow the real parts of the body, not one generic mass). Left and right are always separate parts (midline groove: linea alba, sternum, spine). Split types: 'level' = fraction of the group's own height (0 bottom, 1 top); 'sector' = angle around the limb axis, 0 = front, + = lateral, +-180 = back; 'mask' limits a split to a range of limb position t (0 at the proximal joint, 1 at the distal one). Groups not listed are one block per side; neighbouring groups are always separated (deltoid heads, serratus vs obliques, glutes...). 'tilt' slopes a level cut (+ = descends laterally); 'twist' turns sector cuts along the limb (+ = more lateral at the proximal end).
sources: Gray's Anatomy (public domain 1918 edition): rectus abdominis has three tendinous intersections, at the umbilicus, at the xiphoid process and midway between; pectoralis major clavicular and sternocostal heads; quadriceps rectus femoris between vastus lateralis and vastus medialis; gastrocnemius medial and lateral heads above the soleus; triceps long and lateral heads; serratus anterior digitations.
OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e (CC BY 4.0), chapter 11: axial and appendicular muscles.
profile_comment: Anatomy: separations between different muscles (deltoid/pectoral, deltoid/biceps, serratus/obliques) are the deepest; the linea alba and the spinal groove next; heads of one muscle (pectoral heads, quadriceps, triceps, gastrocnemius) and the abdominal tendinous intersections are shallow. Where a muscle ends in tendon (elbow, knee, wrist, ankle, sternum) it fades into the skin over 3 cm, never as a cut line.
